old: Its deepest root points to something joined or fitted together, not to battle at all.
The Latin word behind it, arma, simply meant tools or equipment.
It shares a Latin ancestor with the English words armature and armure.
clues: This kind of protective gear traces back to an ancient root meaning something like a fitting or joint, the kind of thing that holds a body together.
It is the full covering of metal plates or mail that knights wore into battle, far more complete than a shield. Its Latin ancestor meant equipment or tools.
